history.action: route debug -> implement -> review -> qa (label:bug, confidence 90)

validated_work_order.confidence_rationale: Reproduced end-to-end in a browser against the demo budget, and the arithmetic (week buckets vs the query's date bounds) is verified independently of the UI. The remaining uncertainty is only about which of the two candidate fix sites the maintainers prefer, and whether the same truncation also affects saved reports loaded with an already-week-shaped endDate - both are implementation choices, not open questions about the defect.
validated_work_order.understanding: A custom report on the Weekly interval silently drops 6 of the 7 days of the final week whenever the range is a static (pinned) From/To pair. The From and To pickers both offer week-start dates only, so selecting To: <a Monday/Sunday> produces a query bounded by `date <= <that week-start>`, while the report still renders a full-looking bucket labelled with that week. The chart's last column is therefore a one-day total wearing a seven-day label, and the tooltip's intervalEndDate reports the week-start rather than the week's true last day. Reproduced on this checkout: Weekly + Static, From 08/30/2026 To 09/27/2026 renders five weekly buckets, and the fifth (09/27/2026) reports 23.3px of bar against 230-720px for its siblings; a Daily report starting 09/27/2026 shows 76.93 + 145.24 + 9.26 + 122.08 + 172.18 of spending inside that same week, none of which reaches the weekly bucket.
validated_work_order.root_cause: `validateEnd` in reportRanges.ts returns `dateEnd = end` unchanged for the Weekly interval (the `default:` branch), so the report's `endDate` stays a week-start date. `makeQuery` then filters transactions with `date <= endDate` at day granularity, which admits only the first day of the final week. Meanwhile `weekRangeInclusive` still emits a bucket for that week and custom-spreadsheet/recalculate label its `intervalEndDate` with the raw `endDate`, so the chart shows a complete-looking seven-day column filled from one day. Monthly and Yearly do not exhibit this because their `default`-adjacent branches expand the bound to the period end (`getMonthEnd`, `+ '-12-31'`); Weekly is the only interval whose pickers yield sub-period dates but whose query bound is never widened.
validated_work_order.approach: Widen the effective end bound for the Weekly interval to the true last day of that week, in one shared place, and correct the final bucket's `intervalEndDate` to agree. Preferred site: `validateEnd` in `reportRanges.ts`, adding an explicit `case 'Weekly'` that sets `dateEnd = monthUtils.getWeekEnd(end, firstDayOfWeekIdx)` - the same shape the `Monthly` and `Yearly` branches already use, so the fix is where the interval-specific bound is already normalised. Because `validateEnd` clamps through `boundedRange`, which for Weekly caps `latest` at `monthUtils.currentDay()`, an in-progress week still stops at today rather than projecting into the future. Grep every caller of the function being changed: `validateEnd` is called only from the To: picker in `ReportSidebar.tsx`, and `makeQuery` is called from `fetchSpreadsheetQueryData` (custom + grouped spreadsheets) and `spending-spreadsheet`. The spending report is not affected by the picker path and must not regress. In the same change, set the last interval's `intervalEndDate` to the week's true end in `custom-spreadsheet.ts` and `recalculate.ts` so the tooltip the reporter screenshotted matches the data now included; today those two compute `subDays(intervals[index + 1], 1)` for every bucket except the last, which falls back to the raw `endDate`. If the implementer instead normalises inside `makeQuery`, the same widening must be applied there AND in both spreadsheet files, or the tooltip will keep lying while the data is correct - the two defects share one cause but are two separate wrong values.

files.change: Add an explicit `case 'Weekly'` to `validateEnd` that sets `dateEnd = monthUtils.getWeekEnd(end, firstDayOfWeekIdx)` before the `boundedRange` call, mirroring the existing `Monthly` (`getMonthEnd`) and `Yearly` (`+ '-12-31'`) branches. Keep the `subDays` fallback width consistent with the sibling branches. `validateStart` needs no change: a week-start is already the correct floor for a week bucket.
files.why: The interval-specific bound is already normalised here for every other interval; Weekly is the only one missing, and this is the single point both the From and To pickers funnel through.

files.change: Fix the final interval's `intervalEndDate`: it currently falls back to the raw `endDate` when `index + 1 === intervals.length`, which reports the week-start as the week's end. It must be the true last day of that week (via `monthUtils.getWeekEnd(intervals[index], firstDayOfWeekIdx)`, clamped to `endDate` where the widened bound already caps the range), matching the value `validateEnd` now produces.
files.why: This is the value the reporter screenshotted as wrong in the tooltip and that ReportTableRow passes to the drilldown's `showActivity`; fixing only the query would make the numbers right and the label still wrong.

files.change: Apply the identical last-interval `intervalEndDate` correction as in custom-spreadsheet.ts. The two files carry duplicated copies of this computation and must not diverge.
files.why: Duplicated logic; fixing one and not the other leaves the grouped/table view showing a different range than the graph for the same report.

cases: validateEnd with interval 'Weekly' widens a week-start end bound to that week's last day (2026-09-27 -> 2026-10-03, Sunday-start) - fails today, passes after the fix
validateEnd with interval 'Weekly' and a Monday first-day-of-week widens 2026-09-28 -> 2026-10-04, proving the firstDayOfWeekIdx is honoured rather than hardcoded to Sunday
validateEnd with interval 'Weekly' does not project past today: an end bound in the current week is clamped to currentDay, so no future-dated rows enter the report
validateEnd with interval 'Weekly' respects the earliest-transaction floor (a start before the first transaction is still clamped up)
validateEnd with interval 'Monthly' and 'Yearly' are unchanged by this change (regression guard on the sibling branches)

for Weekly interval with startDate 2026-08-30 and endDate 2026-09-27, the final bucket's intervalEndDate is 2026-10-03 (the week's true end), not 2026-09-27 - encodes the exact value the reporter screenshotted as wrong
for Weekly interval, every non-final bucket's intervalEndDate remains subDays(nextBucket, 1) and is unchanged (08/30 -> 09/05, 09/06 -> 09/12, 09/13 -> 09/19, 09/20 -> 09/26)
for Monthly interval, the final bucket's intervalEndDate is the month's last day, confirming the weekly change did not disturb the monthly branch
a Weekly bucket whose week extends past endDate reports an intervalEndDate equal to endDate rather than a future date

acceptance.check: A custom report with Interval=Weekly and a static From/To pair includes every transaction in the final week, not just the transaction dated on the week-start. On the demo budget, Weekly From 08/30/2026 To 09/27/2026 must report the same total for the 09/27 bucket as a Daily report over 09/27/2026-10/03/2026.
acceptance.how_to_verify: In the app: Reports -> Custom Report, Interval Weekly, Date filters Static, From 08/30/2026, To 09/27/2026, Split Interval. Hover the 09/27/2026 bucket and read its Total. Then switch Interval to Daily, set From 09/27/2026 and To 10/03/2026, and sum the buckets 09/27 through 10/03. Before the fix the weekly bucket is ~1 day of data and the two disagree; after the fix they match.

acceptance.check: The intervalEndDate shown for the final weekly bucket is the last day of that week, not the week-start the user picked. For To: 09/27/2026 it must be 10/03/2026.
acceptance.how_to_verify: Same configuration as AC-1, in Time mode with the Data Table graph. The final column's drilldown/tooltip range must end 10/03/2026. Before the fix it ends 09/27/2026.

acceptance.check: A weekly report whose final week is still in progress stops at today and does not project into future days.
acceptance.how_to_verify: Set Interval Weekly, Date filters Static, To = the current week. Confirm the report's total does not exceed the sum of transactions dated up to today, and that no bucket reports an intervalEndDate later than today.

acceptance.check: The Monthly, Yearly and Daily intervals keep their existing behaviour; only Weekly changes.
acceptance.how_to_verify: Run the same static From/To pair under each of the four intervals and confirm Monthly/Yearly/Daily totals and labels are byte-identical to the same report before the change. Then run `yarn workspace @actual-app/web run test` for the reports unit tests, which include the sibling-branch regression cases in tests[].

acceptance.check: The Spending report is unaffected: it builds its own queries and does not go through the custom report's To: picker.
acceptance.how_to_verify: Run `yarn workspace @actual-app/web run test` and confirm the spending-spreadsheet tests pass. Then load Reports -> Spending with a monthly range and confirm the total matches a pre-change run.

qa_script: yarn start (or use the already-running $PREVIEW_URL at http://localhost:3001), then open the app and choose 'Try the demo' on the onboarding screen to get a budget with transactions.

Navigate to Reports -> Custom Report. Set Interval to Weekly. Under 'Date filters' choose Static (both From: and To: pickers appear, offering week-start dates only - that is the precondition for this bug).
Set From: 08/30/2026 and To: 09/27/2026. Confirm the x-axis renders five weekly buckets: 08/30, 09/06, 09/13, 09/20, 09/27.

AC-1: hover the 09/27/2026 bucket and record its Total. Now switch Interval to Daily, set From  09/27/2026 and To: 10/03/2026, and add up the per-day buckets from 09/27 to 10/03. Before the fix the weekly bucket shows roughly one day of spending (a stub bar, around 1/10 the height of its siblings) and the two figures disagree by hundreds. After the fix they are equal.

AC-2: in Time mode with the Data Table graph, open the final column (09/27/2026) and read its drilldown range. It must end 10/03/2026. On the unfixed build it ends 09/27/2026 - this is the value in the reporter's third screenshot.
AC-3: set To: to the current week. Confirm no intervalEndDate is later than today and the total does not grow when compared with a range ending today.
AC-4: repeat the report under Monthly, Yearly and Daily intervals with the same static bounds and confirm the numbers are unchanged from a pre-change run.
AC-5: load Reports -> Spending for a monthly range and confirm its total is unchanged.
risks: Widening the end bound changes the report's headline total for every existing weekly custom report whose range ends mid-week: totals will go UP, by up to six days of previously-omitted transactions. That is the intended correction, but users who saved weekly reports will see different numbers than before, and any dashboard widget embedding such a report changes with it. This warrants a release note.

If the implementer fixes this in `makeQuery` instead of `validateEnd`, the fix silently applies to the Spending report's four makeQuery call sites too. That path was not exercised by this reproduction; prefer the narrower `validateEnd` site, or verify spending explicitly.

The clamp in `boundedRange` caps Weekly at `currentDay()`, which is what stops an in-progress week from projecting forward. Any fix that bypasses `boundedRange` - normalising inside `makeQuery`, for instance - loses that protection and will pull future-dated rows into reports.
`firstDayOfWeekIdx` is a user preference. `getWeekEnd` honours it, but a hardcoded 6-day offset would silently produce wrong weeks for users whose week starts on another day.
The two duplicated `intervalEndDate` computations (custom-spreadsheet.ts and recalculate.ts) must move together or the graph and the table view will disagree for the same report.
out_of_scope: The Start:/From: side is already correct - a week-start is the right floor for a week bucket - so `validateStart` is deliberately not touched.

Reports other than Custom Report (Spending, Net Worth, Cash Flow, Balance Forecast) do not go through the custom report's static From/To picker and were not observed to exhibit this. Their behaviour is a regression guard, not a target.
The `+1` / `+7` offset buttons and the Live date-range presets are a separate code path (`getSpecificRange`, which already calls `getWeekEnd` for weeks) and are not part of this defect.
evidence: App under test: $PREVIEW_URL=http://localhost:3001 (Actual v26.9.0, local demo budget via 'Try the demo'), reproduced 2026-10-02.

Reproduction steps actually run: Reports -> Custom Report; Interval Monthly -> Weekly; Date filters -> Static; To: 09/27/2026; From: 08/30/2026. The x-axis then renders five buckets: 08/30/2026, 09/06/2026, 09/13/2026, 09/20/2026, 09/27/2026.

Measured weekly bucket totals for that range (bar heights from the rendered recharts SVG, tooltip totals): 08/30 = 1632.87 (721px), 09/06 = 565.15 (230.7px), 09/13 = 569.32 (267.9px), 09/20 = 680.36 (252.3px), 09/27 = 23.3px - a stub roughly 1/10 the height of its siblings, and hovering it produced no category tooltip.

Control measurement, same demo budget, Interval Daily with From: 09/27/2026: per-day totals inside the 09/27 week are 09/27 = 76.93, 09/28 = 145.24, 09/29 = 9.26, 09/30 = 122.08, 10/02 = 172.18. Spending demonstrably exists in that week and none of it appears in the weekly bucket.

Independent arithmetic confirming the mechanism, recomputed outside the UI: weekRangeInclusive('2026-08-30','2026-09-27') = ['2026-08-30','2026-09-06','2026-09-13','2026-09-20','2026-09-27'], so the report renders a fifth bucket, while makeQuery's filter is `date >= 2026-08-30 AND date <= 2026-09-27` - which excludes 2026-09-28, 09-29, 09-30, 10-01, 10-02, 10-03.

The same computation shows the second symptom: for the final bucket, `intervalEndDate` falls back to the raw endDate and reports 2026-09-27, whereas every other bucket correctly reports subDays(nextBucket, 1) (08/30 -> 09/05, 09/06 -> 09/12, 09/13 -> 09/19, 09/20 -> 09/26). Only the last bucket is wrong, matching the reporter's 'intervalEndDate appears wrong here' screenshot.

Code confirmation: reportRanges.ts `validateEnd` has explicit `Monthly` (getMonthEnd) and `Yearly` (+ '-12-31') branches but sends Weekly through `default: dateEnd = end`; makeQuery.ts then filters `{ date: { $transform: '$day', $gte: startDate } } / { $lte: endDate }`. Weekly is the only interval whose pickers yield sub-period dates without widening the bound.

Caller sweep: `validateEnd` is called only from the To: picker in ReportSidebar.tsx; `makeQuery` is called from fetchSpreadsheetQueryData.ts (shared by custom-spreadsheet and grouped-spreadsheet) and spending-spreadsheet.ts. No other caller needs the change.
No console errors were emitted during the reproduction - this is a silent data-truncation defect, not a crash, which is why it survived in a released build.
Scratch Playwright scripts used for the reproduction were deleted; the working tree is clean apart from the untracked plan/ directory.

alternatives_considered.approach: Normalise the end bound inside makeQuery (widen `endDate` to getWeekEnd when interval === 'Weekly').
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It works for the data, but it silently widens the range for all four of Spending's makeQuery call sites, which were never part of this reproduction and could not be verified here. validateEnd is the narrower site and already owns interval-specific bound normalisation for Monthly and Yearly. It also does not fix the intervalEndDate label on its own.

alternatives_considered.approach: Drop the trailing bucket when its week is not fully covered by the range.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: This makes the truncation consistent rather than correct. The reporter's expectation - that the last bucket covers the whole week it is labelled with - is the reasonable one, and dropping the bucket discards a week of data outright. It would also make the bucket count depend on where the range ends, which is surprising.

alternatives_considered.approach: Change the To: picker to offer week-END dates instead of week-starts.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It moves the problem rather than fixing it. weekRangeInclusive already snaps whatever it is given to a week-start, so buckets stay correct, but the stored report's endDate would still be a raw bound the query applies verbatim, and saved reports would keep the old shape. The bound is wrong at the query, not at the picker.

alternatives_considered.approach: Post-process the query results in custom-spreadsheet to redistribute transactions from the excluded days into the final bucket.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The excluded transactions are never fetched - the `$lte` filter runs in SQL against the database. There is nothing downstream to redistribute.

assumptions: The intended semantics are that a Weekly bucket covers the whole week it is labelled with, matching the reporter's expectation and how Monthly/Yearly buckets already behave.

The first day of the week is governed by the user's firstDayOfWeekIdx preference; the fix must read it rather than assume Sunday. The reproduction ran with the default (Sunday), giving 2026-08-30/09-06/... as week-starts.
unknowns: Whether a saved weekly report reloaded with an already-stored week-start endDate re-enters through validateEnd (and so gets normalised on load) or bypasses it and needs normalisation on the load path as well. The debugger reproduced the picker path only; the implementer should check the load path in CustomReport.tsx's `loadReport` handling and cover whichever applies.
Whether the maintainers would rather this landed as a breaking-change release note or be folded into an existing reports fix.
residual_risks: The exact end bound a saved report carries was not verified against the reload path; if it bypasses validateEnd, the picker-only fix would leave already-saved weekly reports still truncated until the user re-picks the range.
